title: Definition
body_md:
A randomized mechanism \( \mathcal{M} \) satisfies \((\epsilon, \delta)\)-differential privacy if, for all adjacent datasets \( D \) and \( D' \) differing in one element, and for all measurable sets \( S \),
\[
\mathbb{P}[\mathcal{M}(D) \in S] \le e^\epsilon \, \mathbb{P}[\mathcal{M}(D') \in S] + \delta.
\]

name: \(\epsilon, \delta\))-Differential Privacy

label: lem:sensitivity_Mg
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:sensitivity_Mg}
Let \(D_g\) and \(D_g'\) be two adjacent local datasets that differ in exactly one sample. Assume that the feature vectors satisfy \(\|x_n\|_2 \le L\) for all \(n\), and let \(M_g^t(D_g)\) denote the client update obtained from the proximal linearized subproblem at iteration \(t\). Then the \(\ell_2\)-sensitivity of the released client update satisfies
\[
\max_{D_g \sim D_g'}
\left\|M_g^t(D_g)-M_g^t(D_g')\right\|_F
\le
\frac{2\sqrt{2}\,L}{N_g\left(\rho+\frac{1}{\eta_g}\right)}.
\]

label: thm:dp_client_update
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:dp_client_update}
Under the assumptions of Lemmas~\ref{lem:sensitivity_Mg} and
\ref{lem:sensitivity_lambda}, consider the perturbed variables
\[
\widetilde{M}_g^t=M_g^t+\xi_g^t,
\qquad
\widetilde{\lambda}_g^t
=\lambda_g^t+\zeta_g^t,
\]
where \(\xi_g^t\sim\mathcal{MN}_{K,P}(0,I_K,\sigma_{M,g}^2 I_P)\) and
\(\zeta_g^t\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma_{\lambda,g}^2)\), with
\[
\sigma_{M,g} =
\frac{2\sqrt{2}L}
{N_g\left(\rho+\frac{1}{\eta_g}\right)}
\frac{\sqrt{2\ln(1.25/\delta_M)}}{\epsilon_M},
\]
and
\[
\sigma_{\lambda,g} =
\frac{\kappa\nu_g}{N_g}
\frac{\sqrt{2\ln(1.25/\delta_\lambda)}}{\epsilon_\lambda}.
\]
Then \(\widetilde{M}_g^t\) satisfies
\((\epsilon_M,\delta_M)\)-differential privacy and
\(\widetilde{\lambda}_g^t\) satisfies
\((\epsilon_\lambda,\delta_\lambda)\)-differential privacy.

title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:sensitivity_Mg}, the local model update
\(M_g^t\) has bounded \(\ell_2\)-sensitivity, and by
Lemma~\ref{lem:sensitivity_lambda}, the local DRO variable
\(\lambda_g^t\) has bounded sensitivity. Applying the Gaussian
mechanism \cite[Theorem~3.22]{dwork2014algorithmic} separately
to each variable, with noise calibrated to its corresponding
sensitivity, yields the stated privacy guarantees for
\(\widetilde{M}_g^t\) and \(\widetilde{\lambda}_g^t\).

title: Results
body_md: For this dataset, we examine the privacy--utility tradeoff and convergence behavior. Figure~\ref{fig:privacy_tradeoff} shows the effect of the privacy hyperparameters on model performance, with the cumulative budget $\bar{\epsilon}$ on the top axis. At the smallest per-round budget, $\epsilon=0.01$, the injected noise dominates the signal and all private models perform poorly with large variability across seeds. As $\epsilon$ increases, all three private models improve, since larger values of $\epsilon$ correspond to weaker privacy guarantees and lower injected noise, and DP-Fed DRO and DP-Fed SGD approach the non-private Fed DRO model. DP-Fed ERM, in contrast, saturates early and does not benefit from larger budgets. DP-Fed DRO is the best private method at every budget where the models are informative, with the clearest margin at moderate budgets, $\epsilon\in\{0.05,0.1\}$, where the noise is significant but does not overwhelm the signal. DP-Fed DRO is also markedly more robust to the choice of $\delta$ than DP-Fed SGD, whose performance degrades noticeably as $\delta$ tightens. As a result, the gap between the two is largest at the tightest values of $\delta$. This reflects the ability of the robust formulation to absorb the larger noise level induced by a smaller $\delta$ with little loss in performance.

title: Results
body_md: Table~\ref{tab:uci_main_results} summarizes the Macro-F1 scores on the five multiclass benchmark datasets. Among the private methods, DP-Fed DRO achieves the best performance on Iris, Wine, and Seeds, with the clearest margins on Wine and Seeds, and ranks second on Palmer Penguins, giving it the strongest performance overall across the five datasets. DP-Fed ERM performs best on Palmer Penguins and DP-Fed SGD on Dermatology, so no single private baseline is consistently competitive, whereas DP-Fed DRO remains among the top private methods on most datasets. Notably, the three datasets on which DP-Fed DRO performs best are also the smallest, where each client holds the fewest samples. Since the sensitivity of the local updates scales inversely with the local sample size, these are the settings with the largest injected noise, suggesting that the robust formulation is most beneficial when the privacy-induced perturbations are most severe. Compared with the non-private models, privacy incurs a substantial cost on all datasets, most notably on Iris and Dermatology. This is expected under such strict privacy conditions, where each client holds only a few dozen samples and therefore requires large noise to protect each one. The non-private results also show that the native multiclass and OvA DRO formulations have mixed behavior across real datasets, with native multiclass Fed DRO performing better on Iris, OvA Fed DRO performing better on Dermatology, and both performing similarly on the remaining datasets. We therefore use a controlled synthetic study, presented in Appendix~\ref{app:synthetic_overlap}, to identify when the native multiclass formulation is most useful relative to OvA. The results show that its advantage is most evident when related fault classes have correlated features and partial overlap, so that the classes are difficult to separate but not completely inseparable.

title: Results
body_md: The results are presented in Figure~\ref{fig:scalability_summary}. In the fixed-total-sample setting, the runtime required to reach peak mCCR remains relatively stable for the private models as the number of clients increases. Thus, adding clients does not substantially increase the runtime when the total dataset size is fixed. For the Non-Private Fed DRO baseline, the runtime decreases initially and then stabilizes, which is consistent with the fact that each client receives fewer local samples as \(G\) increases and the local DRO subproblems become smaller. Across all values of \(G\), Non-Private Fed DRO remains the most expensive method by at least an order of magnitude, because each round requires solving local DRO optimization subproblems, whereas the private models rely on simpler local updates. Among the private models, DP-Fed DRO is slower than DP-Fed ERM and DP-Fed SGD by a roughly constant factor, reflecting the additional terms introduced by the DRO formulation.

label: eq:sens_pf_optimality
title: Proof
body_md:
Consider the proximal linearized client subproblem in
\eqref{eq:prox_linearized_lagrangian}. To make the dependence
on the local dataset explicit, denote the nonsmooth term in
\eqref{eq:def_f_local} by $f(M_g,\lambda_g;D_g).$
The first-order optimality condition for the update \(M_g^t(D_g)\)
with respect to \(M_g\) is
\begin{equation}
0 \in \partial_{M_g} f\!\left( \widetilde M_g^{t-1}, \widetilde{\lambda}_g^{t-1}; D_g \right) + \rho\left( M_g^t(D_g)-M^{t-1}+\mu_g^{t-1} \right) + \frac{1}{\eta_g} \left( M_g^t(D_g)-\widetilde M_g^{t-1} \right).
\label{eq:sens_pf_optimality}
\end{equation}
Equivalently,
\begin{equation}
\left( \rho+\frac{1}{\eta_g} \right) M_g^t(D_g) = - \partial_{M_g} f\!\left( \widetilde M_g^{t-1}, \widetilde{\lambda}_g^{t-1}; D_g \right) + \rho\left( M^{t-1}-\mu_g^{t-1} \right) + \frac{1}{\eta_g} \widetilde M_g^{t-1}.
\label{eq:sens_pf_update}
\end{equation}

Let \(D_g\sim D_g'\) be adjacent local datasets differing in
exactly one sample, indexed by \(j\). We condition on the
algorithmic state available at the beginning of iteration
\(t\), including the previous perturbed variables and server
broadcasts. Thus, \(M^{t-1}\), \(\mu_g^{t-1}\),
\(\widetilde M_g^{t-1}\),
\(\widetilde{\lambda}_g^{t-1}\), and
\(\tau_g^{t-1}\) are fixed when comparing the current update
under \(D_g\) and \(D_g'\). In particular, \(\tau_g^{t-1}\)
is computed from the previous perturbed variables according to
Algorithm~\ref{alg:dp_fed_dro}.

Under this fixed algorithmic state, the quadratic terms and the
linearized Bertsekas penalty contribution are identical for
the two adjacent datasets. Moreover, the robust-loss
contributions associated with all unchanged samples are
identical. Hence, the only difference in
\eqref{eq:sens_pf_update} arises from the single changed sample
in the empirical robust-loss average. Therefore,
\begin{equation}
M_g^t(D_g)-M_g^t(D_g') = -\left(\rho+\frac{1}{\eta_g}\right)^{-1} \frac{1}{N_g} \Bigl( \partial_{M_g}\ell_j^{(g)}(D_g) - \partial_{M_g}\ell_j^{(g)}(D_g') \Bigr),
\label{eq:sens_pf_difference}
\end{equation}
where
\(\partial_{M_g}\ell_j^{(g)}(D_g)\) and
\(\partial_{M_g}\ell_j^{(g)}(D_g')\)
denote selected subgradients of the robust-loss contribution
associated with the differing sample under \(D_g\) and \(D_g'\),
respectively.

For the multiclass Crammer--Singer loss, any active \(M_g\)-subgradient has the form
\begin{equation}
\left(v_{(c)}-y\right)x^\top
\label{eq:sens_pf_subgradient_form}
\end{equation}
for an active class \(c\neq y\). At points where multiple
classes are active, the subdifferential is the convex hull of
such matrices.

Using $\|ab^\top\|_F=\|a\|_2\|b\|_2,$
the one-hot encoding property
$\|v_{(c)}-y\|_2=\sqrt{2},$
and the bounded-feature assumption \(\|x\|_2\leq L\), we obtain
\begin{equation}
\left\|
\partial_{M_g}\ell_j^{(g)}(D_g)
\right\|_F
\leq \sqrt{2}L,
\qquad
\left\|
\partial_{M_g}\ell_j^{(g)}(D_g')
\right\|_F
\leq \sqrt{2}L.
\label{eq:sens_pf_subgradient_bound}
\end{equation}

Applying the triangle inequality to
\eqref{eq:sens_pf_difference} and then using
\eqref{eq:sens_pf_subgradient_bound} yields
\begin{align}
\left\| M_g^t(D_g)-M_g^t(D_g') \right\|_F
&\leq \left( \rho+\frac{1}{\eta_g} \right)^{-1} \frac{1}{N_g} \Bigl( \left\| \partial_{M_g}\ell_j^{(g)}(D_g) \right\|_F + \left\| \partial_{M_g}\ell_j^{(g)}(D_g') \right\|_F \Bigr) \notag\\
&\leq \frac{2\sqrt{2}L}{N_g\left(\rho+1/\eta_g\right)}.
\label{eq:sens_pf_final}
\end{align}
Taking the maximum over all adjacent datasets
\(D_g\sim D_g'\) yields the desired sensitivity bound.

title: Proof
body_md:
As in Lemma~\ref{lem:sensitivity_Mg}, condition on the algorithmic
state available at the beginning of iteration \(t\). The first-order
optimality condition for the \(\lambda_g\)-update gives
\[
\lambda_g^t(D_g)
=
\widetilde{\lambda}_g^{t-1}
-
\nu_g
\left(
r_g+
\partial_{\lambda_g}
f\!\left(
\widetilde M_g^{t-1},
\widetilde{\lambda}_g^{t-1};
D_g
\right)
\right).
\]

Let \(D_g\sim D_g'\) differ in exactly one sample, indexed by
\(j\). Subtracting the two updates,
\begin{equation}
\left| \lambda_g^t(D_g)-\lambda_g^t(D_g') \right| = \nu_g \left| \partial_{\lambda_g} f\!\left( \widetilde M_g^{t-1}, \widetilde{\lambda}_g^{t-1}; D_g \right) - \partial_{\lambda_g} f\!\left( \widetilde M_g^{t-1}, \widetilde{\lambda}_g^{t-1}; D_g' \right) \right|.
\label{eq:sens_lambda_difference}
\end{equation}

Under the fixed algorithmic state, the Bertsekas penalty
contribution and the robust-loss contributions associated with
all unchanged samples are identical under \(D_g\) and \(D_g'\).
Hence, only the differing sample contributes, so that
\begin{align}
\left|
\lambda_g^t(D_g)-\lambda_g^t(D_g')
\right|
&\le
\frac{\nu_g}{N_g}
\left|
\partial_{\lambda_g}\ell_j^{(g)}(D_g)
-
\partial_{\lambda_g}\ell_j^{(g)}(D_g')
\right|.
\end{align}

For each sample, the robust-loss subgradient with respect to
\(\lambda_g\) satisfies
\[
\partial_{\lambda_g}
\ell_n^{(g)}(M_g,\lambda_g)
\in[-\kappa,0].
\]
Therefore,
\[
\left|
\partial_{\lambda_g}\ell_j^{(g)}(D_g)
-
\partial_{\lambda_g}\ell_j^{(g)}(D_g')
\right|
\le
\kappa,
\]
which yields
\[
\left|
\lambda_g^t(D_g)-\lambda_g^t(D_g')
\right|
\le
\frac{\kappa\nu_g}{N_g}.
\]
Taking the maximum over all adjacent datasets gives the result.

title: Proof
body_md:
For any client \(g\), let \(h_g^t(\cdot):=h_g(\cdot;\tau_g^{t-1})\). Since \(h_g^t\) is convex in \(z_g\), we have the subgradient inequality
\begin{equation}
h_g^t(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})-h_g^t(z_g)\le\big\langle h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1}),\,\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1}-z_g\big\rangle .
\end{equation}

Adding the scaled-dual consensus term to both sides yields

\begin{equation}
h_g^t(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})-h_g^t(z_g)
+\rho\langle \widetilde M_g^t-M_g,\mu_g^t\rangle_F
\le
\big\langle h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1}),
\,\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1}-z_g \big\rangle
+\rho\langle \widetilde M_g^t-M_g,\mu_g^t\rangle_F .
\label{eq:lem1_app_2}
\end{equation}

Define the padded dual variable $\bar\mu_g^t := (\mu_g^t,0)$.
Expanding $\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1}-z_g
=
(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1}-\widetilde z_g^t)+(\widetilde z_g^t-z_g),$
we obtain
\begin{equation}
\left\langle h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1}),
\,\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1}-z_g \right\rangle
+\rho\langle \widetilde M_g^t-M_g,\mu_g^t\rangle_F
=
\left\langle h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1}),
\,\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1}-\widetilde z_g^t \right\rangle
+\left\langle h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})+\rho\bar\mu_g^t,
\,\widetilde z_g^t-z_g \right\rangle .
\label{eq:lem1_app_3}
\end{equation}


Define also the padded noise variables $\bar\xi_g^t := (\xi_g^t,0)$ and $\bar\zeta_g^t := (0,\zeta_g^t).$
For coefficients \(c_k\) and \(c_\ell\) specified below, adding and subtracting
\(c_k\bar\xi_g^t+c_\ell\bar\zeta_g^t\) in both inner products gives
\begin{multline}
\left\langle h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1}),
\,\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1}-\widetilde z_g^t \right\rangle
+\left\langle h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})+\rho\bar\mu_g^t,
\,\widetilde z_g^t-z_g \right\rangle
\\
=
\left\langle
h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})
-c_k\bar\xi_g^t
-c_\ell\bar\zeta_g^t,\,
\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1}-\widetilde z_g^t
\right\rangle
\\
\qquad
-c_k\langle \xi_g^t,\,
M_g-\widetilde M_g^{\,t-1}\rangle_F
-c_\ell\zeta_g^t
\bigl(\lambda_g-\widetilde\lambda_g^{\,t-1}\bigr)
\\
\qquad
+\left\langle
h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})
+\rho\bar\mu_g^t
-c_k\bar\xi_g^t
-c_\ell\bar\zeta_g^t,\,
\widetilde z_g^t-z_g
\right\rangle .
\label{eq:lem1_app_4}
\end{multline}


Using the scaled-dual update
\(\bar\mu_g^t=\bar\mu_g^{t-1}+(\widetilde M_g^t-M^t,0)\)
and the decomposition
\[
(\widetilde M_g^t-M^t,0)
=
(\widetilde M_g^t-M^{t-1},0)
+
(M^{t-1}-M^t,0),
\]
we obtain
\begin{multline}
\left\langle
h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})
-c_k\bar\xi_g^t
-c_\ell\bar\zeta_g^t,\,
\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1}-\widetilde z_g^t
\right\rangle
\\
-c_k\langle \xi_g^t,\,
M_g-\widetilde M_g^{\,t-1}\rangle_F
-c_\ell\zeta_g^t
\bigl(\lambda_g-\widetilde\lambda_g^{\,t-1}\bigr)
\\
+\left\langle
h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})
+\rho\bar\mu_g^t
-c_k\bar\xi_g^t
-c_\ell\bar\zeta_g^t,\,
\widetilde z_g^t-z_g
\right\rangle
\\
=
\left\langle
h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})
-c_k\bar\xi_g^t
-c_\ell\bar\zeta_g^t,\,
\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1}-\widetilde z_g^t
\right\rangle
\\
-c_k\langle \xi_g^t,\,
M_g-\widetilde M_g^{\,t-1}\rangle_F
-c_\ell\zeta_g^t
\bigl(\lambda_g-\widetilde\lambda_g^{\,t-1}\bigr)
\\
+\left\langle
h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})
+\rho \bar\mu_g^{\,t-1}
+\rho(\widetilde M_g^t-M^{t-1},0)
-c_k\bar\xi_g^t
-c_\ell\bar\zeta_g^t,\,
\widetilde z_g^t-z_g
\right\rangle
\\
+\rho\langle
\widetilde M_g^t-M_g,\,
M^{t-1}-M^t
\rangle_F .
\label{eq:lem1_app_5}
\end{multline}


We now upper bound the last term in \eqref{eq:lem1_app_5} by rewriting the inner product as a difference of squared Frobenius norms.  
Using the identity
\begin{equation}
\|A-C\|_F^2 = \|A-B\|_F^2+\|B-C\|_F^2+2\langle A-B,\;B-C\rangle_F,
\label{eq:basic_frob_expand}
\end{equation}
we first apply \eqref{eq:basic_frob_expand} with $
(A,B,C)=(M_g,M^t,M^{t-1}), $
which gives
\begin{equation}
\|M_g-M^{t-1}\|_F^2
=
\|M_g-M^t\|_F^2+\|M^t-M^{t-1}\|_F^2
+2\langle M_g-M^t,\;M^t-M^{t-1}\rangle_F.
\label{eq:lem1_app_sq1}
\end{equation}
Next, apply \eqref{eq:basic_frob_expand} with
$(A,B,C)=(\widetilde M_g^t,M^t,M^{t-1}),$
which yields
\begin{equation}
\|\widetilde M_g^t-M^{t-1}\|_F^2
=
\|\widetilde M_g^t-M^t\|_F^2+\|M^t-M^{t-1}\|_F^2
+2\langle \widetilde M_g^t-M^t,\;M^t-M^{t-1}\rangle_F.
\label{eq:lem1_app_sq2}
\end{equation}
Subtracting \eqref{eq:lem1_app_sq1} from \eqref{eq:lem1_app_sq2}, the common term
\(\|M^t-M^{t-1}\|_F^2\) cancels, and we obtain
\begin{equation}
2\langle \widetilde M_g^t-M_g,\;M^{t-1}-M^t\rangle_F
=
\|M_g-M^{t-1}\|_F^2-\|M_g-M^t\|_F^2
+\|\widetilde M_g^t-M^t\|_F^2-\|\widetilde M_g^t-M^{t-1}\|_F^2.
\label{eq:lem1_app_sq3}
\end{equation}
Multiplying by \(\rho/2\) and dropping the final nonpositive term gives
\begin{equation}
\rho\langle \widetilde M_g^t-M_g,\;M^{t-1}-M^t\rangle_F
\le
\frac{\rho}{2}
\Big(
\|M_g-M^{t-1}\|_F^2-\|M_g-M^t\|_F^2
\Big)
+\frac{\rho}{2}\|\widetilde M_g^t-M^t\|_F^2.
\end{equation}
Finally, using the scaled dual update
\[
\mu_g^t-\mu_g^{t-1}=\widetilde M_g^t-M^t,
\]
we conclude that
\begin{equation}
\rho\langle \widetilde M_g^t-M_g,\;M^{t-1}-M^t\rangle_F
\le
\frac{\rho}{2}
\Big(
\|M_g-M^{t-1}\|_F^2-\|M_g-M^t\|_F^2
\Big)
+\frac{\rho}{2}\|\mu_g^t-\mu_g^{t-1}\|_F^2 .
\label{eq:lem1_app_6}
\end{equation}

Set $c_k:=\rho+\frac{1}{\eta_g},$ and $c_\ell:=\frac{1}{\nu_g}.$
We now split the second-to-last term in \eqref{eq:lem1_app_5}
into its \(M\)- and \(\lambda\)-components. Since $\bar\mu_g^{\,t-1}=(\mu_g^{t-1},0),\bar\xi_g^t=(\xi_g^t,0), $ and $ \bar\zeta_g^t=(0,\zeta_g^t),$
we have
\begin{multline}
\left\langle
h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})
+\rho \bar\mu_g^{\,t-1}
+\rho(\widetilde M_g^t-M^{t-1},0)
-c_k\bar\xi_g^t
-c_\ell\bar\zeta_g^t,\,
\widetilde z_g^t-z_g
\right\rangle
\\
=
\left\langle
[h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})]_M
+\rho(\widetilde M_g^t-M^{t-1}+\mu_g^{t-1})
-\left(\rho+\frac{1}{\eta_g}\right)\xi_g^t,\,
\widetilde M_g^t-M_g
\right\rangle_F
\\
\qquad
+
\left(
[h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})]_{\lambda}
-\frac{1}{\nu_g}\zeta_g^t
\right)
(\widetilde\lambda_g^t-\lambda_g).
\label{eq:lem1_app_7split}
\end{multline}


Applying Lemma~5 of \citet{huang2019dp} to the \(M\)-block term in \eqref{eq:lem1_app_7split}, with $D(X,Y)=\frac12\|X-Y\|_F^2 $ and $
s=\frac{1}{\eta_g},$
yields
\begin{multline}
\left\langle
[h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})]_M
+\rho(\widetilde M_g^t-M^{t-1}+\mu_g^{t-1})
-\left(\rho+\frac{1}{\eta_g}\right)\xi_g^t,\,
\widetilde M_g^t-M_g
\right\rangle_F
\\
\le
\frac{1}{2\eta_g}
\Big(
\|M_g-\widetilde M_g^{\,t-1}\|_F^2
-\|M_g-\widetilde M_g^t\|_F^2
-\|\widetilde M_g^t-\widetilde M_g^{\,t-1}\|_F^2
\Big).
\label{eq:lem1_app_7M}
\end{multline}

Applying Lemma~5 of \citet{huang2019dp} to the \(\lambda\)-block, with
$D(x,y)=\frac12(x-y)^2$ and
$s=\frac{1}{\nu_g},$
yields
\begin{equation}
\left(
[h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})]_{\lambda}
-\frac{1}{\nu_g}\zeta_g^t
\right)
(\widetilde\lambda_g^t-\lambda_g)
\le
\frac{1}{2\nu_g}
\Big(
(\lambda_g-\widetilde\lambda_g^{t-1})^2
-(\lambda_g-\widetilde\lambda_g^t)^2
-(\widetilde\lambda_g^t-\widetilde\lambda_g^{t-1})^2
\Big).
\label{eq:lem1_app_7lambda}
\end{equation}

Combining \eqref{eq:lem1_app_7split}, \eqref{eq:lem1_app_7M},
and \eqref{eq:lem1_app_7lambda}, we obtain
\begin{multline}
\left\langle
h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})
+\rho \bar\mu_g^{\,t-1}
+\rho(\widetilde M_g^t-M^{t-1},0)
-\left(\rho+\frac{1}{\eta_g}\right)\bar\xi_g^t
-\frac{1}{\nu_g}\bar\zeta_g^t,\,
\widetilde z_g^t-z_g
\right\rangle
\\
\le
\frac{1}{2\eta_g}
\Big(
\|M_g-\widetilde M_g^{\,t-1}\|_F^2
-\|M_g-\widetilde M_g^t\|_F^2
-\|\widetilde M_g^t-\widetilde M_g^{\,t-1}\|_F^2
\Big)
\\
\qquad
+
\frac{1}{2\nu_g}
\Big(
(\lambda_g-\widetilde\lambda_g^{\,t-1})^2
-(\lambda_g-\widetilde\lambda_g^t)^2
-(\widetilde\lambda_g^t-\widetilde\lambda_g^{\,t-1})^2
\Big).
\label{eq:lem1_app_7full}
\end{multline}


Then, using the block decomposition
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
&\left\langle
h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})
-\left(\rho+\frac{1}{\eta_g}\right)\bar\xi_g^t
-\frac{1}{\nu_g}\bar\zeta_g^t,\,
\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1}-\widetilde z_g^t
\right\rangle
\\
&=
\left\langle
[h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})]_M
-\left(\rho+\frac{1}{\eta_g}\right)\xi_g^t,\,
\widetilde M_g^{\,t-1}-\widetilde M_g^t
\right\rangle_F
\\
&\qquad
+
\left(
[h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})]_\lambda
-\frac{1}{\nu_g}\zeta_g^t
\right)
(\widetilde\lambda_g^{\,t-1}-\widetilde\lambda_g^t),
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:lem1_app_8split}
\end{equation}
and applying Cauchy--Schwarz and Young's inequality blockwise, we obtain
\begin{multline}
\left\langle
h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})
-\left(\rho+\frac{1}{\eta_g}\right)\bar\xi_g^t
-\frac{1}{\nu_g}\bar\zeta_g^t,\,
\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1}-\widetilde z_g^t
\right\rangle
\\
\le
\frac{\eta_g}{2}
\left\|
[h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})]_M
-\left(\rho+\frac{1}{\eta_g}\right)\xi_g^t
\right\|_F^2
+
\frac{1}{2\eta_g}
\|\widetilde M_g^t-\widetilde M_g^{\,t-1}\|_F^2
\\
\qquad
+
\frac{\nu_g}{2}
\left|
[h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})]_\lambda
-\frac{1}{\nu_g}\zeta_g^t
\right|^2
+
\frac{1}{2\nu_g}
(\widetilde\lambda_g^t-\widetilde\lambda_g^{\,t-1})^2 .
\label{eq:lem1_app_8full}
\end{multline}


Combining the previous three upper bounds, we obtain
\begin{multline}
h_g^t(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})-h_g^t(z_g)
+\rho\langle \widetilde M_g^t-M_g,\mu_g^t\rangle_F
\\
\le
\frac{\eta_g}{2}
\left\|
[h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})]_M
-\left(\rho+\frac{1}{\eta_g}\right)\xi_g^t
\right\|_F^2
\\
\qquad
+\frac{\nu_g}{2}
\left|
[h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})]_\lambda
-\frac{1}{\nu_g}\zeta_g^t
\right|^2
\\
\qquad
-\left(\rho+\frac{1}{\eta_g}\right)
\langle \xi_g^t,\,
M_g-\widetilde M_g^{\,t-1}\rangle_F
\\
\qquad
-\frac{1}{\nu_g}\zeta_g^t
\bigl(\lambda_g-\widetilde\lambda_g^{\,t-1}\bigr)
\\
\qquad
+\frac{1}{2\eta_g}
\Big(
\|M_g-\widetilde M_g^{\,t-1}\|_F^2
-\|M_g-\widetilde M_g^t\|_F^2
\Big)
\\
\qquad
+\frac{1}{2\nu_g}
\Big(
(\lambda_g-\widetilde\lambda_g^{\,t-1})^2
-(\lambda_g-\widetilde\lambda_g^t)^2
\Big)
\\
\qquad
+\frac{\rho}{2}
\Big(
\|M_g-M^{t-1}\|_F^2
-\|M_g-M^{t}\|_F^2
\Big)
+\frac{\rho}{2}
\|\mu_g^t-\mu_g^{t-1}\|_F^2 .
\label{eq:lem1_app_9}
\end{multline}


For each client \(g\), add the terms
\[
-\rho\langle \mu_g^t,\;M^t-M\rangle_F
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\rho\langle \mu_g-\mu_g^t,\;\widetilde M_g^t-M^t\rangle_F
\]
to both sides of \eqref{eq:lem1_app_9}. Then, weighting by \(\alpha_g\) and summing over \(g=1,\dots,G\), we arrive at
\begin{align}
\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
&\Big(
h_g^t(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})-h_g^t(z_g)
+\rho\langle \widetilde M_g^t-M_g,\mu_g^t\rangle_F
\notag\\
&\qquad
-\rho\langle \mu_g^t,\,
M^t-M\rangle_F
+\rho\langle \mu_g-\mu_g^t,\,
\widetilde M_g^t-M^t\rangle_F
\Big)
\notag\\
&\le
\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\Bigg[
\frac{\eta_g}{2}
\left\|
[h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})]_M
-\left(\rho+\frac{1}{\eta_g}\right)\xi_g^t
\right\|_F^2
\notag\\
&\qquad
+\frac{\nu_g}{2}
\left|
[h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})]_\lambda
-\frac{1}{\nu_g}\zeta_g^t
\right|^2
\notag\\
&\qquad
-\left(\rho+\frac{1}{\eta_g}\right)
\langle \xi_g^t,\,
M_g-\widetilde M_g^{\,t-1}\rangle_F
\notag\\
&\qquad
-\frac{1}{\nu_g}\zeta_g^t
\bigl(\lambda_g-\widetilde\lambda_g^{\,t-1}\bigr)
\notag\\
&\qquad
+\frac{1}{2\eta_g}
\Big(
\|M_g-\widetilde M_g^{\,t-1}\|_F^2
-\|M_g-\widetilde M_g^t\|_F^2
\Big)
\notag\\
&\qquad
+\frac{1}{2\nu_g}
\Big(
(\lambda_g-\widetilde\lambda_g^{\,t-1})^2
-(\lambda_g-\widetilde\lambda_g^t)^2
\Big)
\notag\\
&\qquad
+\frac{\rho}{2}
\Big(
\|M_g-M^{t-1}\|_F^2
-\|M_g-M^{t}\|_F^2
\Big)
+\frac{\rho}{2}\|\mu_g^t-\mu_g^{t-1}\|_F^2
\notag\\
&\qquad
-\rho\langle \mu_g^t,\,
M^t-M\rangle_F
+\rho\langle \mu_g-\mu_g^t,\,
\widetilde M_g^t-M^t\rangle_F
\Bigg].
\label{eq:lem1_app_10}
\end{align}



Next, using the dual update and the server aggregation rule, we obtain the identities in \eqref{eq:lem1_app_11} and \eqref{eq:lem1_app_12}. In particular, \eqref{eq:lem1_app_11} follows from the fact that the weighted dual average is zero, while \eqref{eq:lem1_app_12} follows by substituting
$\widetilde M_g^t-M^t=\mu_g^t-\mu_g^{t-1}$
and expanding the squared Frobenius norm:
\begin{equation}
\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g \langle M^t-M,\mu_g^t\rangle_F
=
\left\langle
M^t-M,\,
\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g\mu_g^t
\right\rangle_F
=0 ,
\label{eq:lem1_app_11}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
\langle \mu_g-\mu_g^t,\,
\widetilde M_g^t-M^t\rangle_F
=
\langle \mu_g-\mu_g^t,\,
\mu_g^t-\mu_g^{t-1}\rangle_F
=
\frac{1}{2}
\Big(
\|\mu_g-\mu_g^{t-1}\|_F^2
-\|\mu_g-\mu_g^t\|_F^2
-\|\mu_g^t-\mu_g^{t-1}\|_F^2
\Big).
\label{eq:lem1_app_12}
\end{equation}
Substituting \eqref{eq:lem1_app_11} and \eqref{eq:lem1_app_12}
into \eqref{eq:lem1_app_10}, the term
$\frac{\rho}{2}\|\mu_g^t-\mu_g^{t-1}\|_F^2$
cancels with the last term in \eqref{eq:lem1_app_12}, and we obtain
\begin{multline}
\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\Big(
h_g^t(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})-h_g^t(z_g)
+\rho\langle \widetilde M_g^t-M_g,\mu_g^t\rangle_F
\\
\qquad
+\rho\langle \mu_g-\mu_g^t,\,
\widetilde M_g^t-M^t\rangle_F
\Big)
\\
\le
\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\Bigg[
\frac{\eta_g}{2}
\left\|
[h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})]_M
-\left(\rho+\frac{1}{\eta_g}\right)\xi_g^t
\right\|_F^2
\\
\qquad
+\frac{\nu_g}{2}
\left|
[h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})]_\lambda
-\frac{1}{\nu_g}\zeta_g^t
\right|^2
\\
\qquad
-\left(\rho+\frac{1}{\eta_g}\right)
\langle \xi_g^t,\,
M_g-\widetilde M_g^{\,t-1}\rangle_F
\\
\qquad
-\frac{1}{\nu_g}\zeta_g^t
\bigl(\lambda_g-\widetilde\lambda_g^{\,t-1}\bigr)
\\
\qquad
+\frac{1}{2\eta_g}
\Big(
\|M_g-\widetilde M_g^{\,t-1}\|_F^2
-\|M_g-\widetilde M_g^t\|_F^2
\Big)
\\
\qquad
+\frac{1}{2\nu_g}
\Big(
(\lambda_g-\widetilde\lambda_g^{\,t-1})^2
-(\lambda_g-\widetilde\lambda_g^t)^2
\Big)
\\
\qquad
+\frac{\rho}{2}
\Big(
\|M_g-M^{t-1}\|_F^2
-\|M_g-M^{t}\|_F^2
\Big)
\\
\qquad
+\frac{\rho}{2}
\Big(
\|\mu_g-\mu_g^{t-1}\|_F^2
-\|\mu_g-\mu_g^t\|_F^2
\Big)
\Bigg].
\label{eq:lem1_app_13}
\end{multline}

label: lem:coercive
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:coercive}
For each client $g$, assume that
\[
\eta_g>0,\qquad \nu_g>0,\qquad \rho>0.
\]
Then, for each iteration $t$, the proximal linearized surrogate $\widehat L_{\rho,g}^t(M_g,\lambda_g)$ is coercive in $(M_g,\lambda_g)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Recall that
\begin{multline}
\widehat L_{\rho,g}^t(M_g,\lambda_g)
=
f(\widetilde M_g^{t-1},\widetilde\lambda_g^{t-1})
+
\left\langle \partial_{M_g} f(\widetilde M_g^{t-1},\widetilde\lambda_g^{t-1}),\, M_g-\widetilde M_g^{t-1}\right\rangle_F
\\
+
\left\langle \partial_{\lambda_g} f(\widetilde M_g^{t-1},\widetilde\lambda_g^{t-1}),\, \lambda_g-\widetilde\lambda_g^{t-1}\right\rangle
+
\lambda_g r_g
+
\frac{\rho}{2}\left\|M_g-M^{t-1}+\mu_g^{t-1}\right\|_F^2
\\
+
\frac{1}{2\eta_g}\left\|M_g-\widetilde M_g^{t-1}\right\|_F^2
+
\frac{1}{2\nu_g}\left(\lambda_g-\widetilde\lambda_g^{t-1}\right)^2 .
\end{multline}

The term $f(\widetilde M_g^{t-1},\widetilde\lambda_g^{t-1})$ is constant with respect to $(M_g,\lambda_g)$ and therefore does not affect coercivity.

We first expand the terms depending on $M_g$. We have
\begin{equation}
\left\langle \partial_{M_g} f(\widetilde M_g^{t-1},\widetilde\lambda_g^{t-1}),\, M_g-\widetilde M_g^{t-1}\right\rangle_F
=
\left\langle \partial_{M_g} f(\widetilde M_g^{t-1},\widetilde\lambda_g^{t-1}),\, M_g\right\rangle_F
\\
-
\left\langle \partial_{M_g} f(\widetilde M_g^{t-1},\widetilde\lambda_g^{t-1}),\, \widetilde M_g^{t-1}\right\rangle_F ,
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
\frac{1}{2\eta_g}\left\|M_g-\widetilde M_g^{t-1}\right\|_F^2
=
\frac{1}{2\eta_g}\|M_g\|_F^2
-
\frac{1}{\eta_g}\left\langle M_g,\widetilde M_g^{t-1}\right\rangle_F
\\
+
\frac{1}{2\eta_g}\left\|\widetilde M_g^{t-1}\right\|_F^2 ,
\end{equation}
while
\begin{equation}
\frac{\rho}{2}\left\|M_g-M^{t-1}+\mu_g^{t-1}\right\|_F^2
=
\frac{\rho}{2}\|M_g\|_F^2
-
\rho\left\langle M_g,\, M^{t-1}-\mu_g^{t-1}\right\rangle_F
\\
+
\frac{\rho}{2}\left\|M^{t-1}-\mu_g^{t-1}\right\|_F^2 .
\end{equation}

Therefore, all terms independent of \(M_g\) can be grouped into \(B_g^t\), and
\(\widehat L_{\rho,g}^t(M_g,\lambda_g)\) can be written as
\begin{equation}
\left(\frac{1}{2\eta_g}+\frac{\rho}{2}\right)\|M_g\|_F^2
+
\Bigl\langle
\partial_{M_g} f(\widetilde M_g^{t-1},\widetilde\lambda_g^{t-1})
-
\frac{1}{\eta_g}\widetilde M_g^{t-1}
\\
-
\rho\bigl(M^{t-1}-\mu_g^{t-1}\bigr),
\, M_g
\Bigr\rangle_F
+
B_g^t.
\end{equation}

Next, we expand the terms depending on $\lambda_g$. We have
\begin{equation}
\left\langle \partial_{\lambda_g} f(\widetilde M_g^{t-1},\widetilde\lambda_g^{t-1}),\, \lambda_g-\widetilde\lambda_g^{t-1}\right\rangle
=
\partial_{\lambda_g} f(\widetilde M_g^{t-1},\widetilde\lambda_g^{t-1})\,\lambda_g
\\
-
\partial_{\lambda_g} f(\widetilde M_g^{t-1},\widetilde\lambda_g^{t-1})\,\widetilde\lambda_g^{t-1},
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
\frac{1}{2\nu_g}\left(\lambda_g-\widetilde\lambda_g^{t-1}\right)^2
=
\frac{1}{2\nu_g}\lambda_g^2
-
\frac{1}{\nu_g}\widetilde\lambda_g^{t-1}\lambda_g
+
\frac{1}{2\nu_g}\left(\widetilde\lambda_g^{t-1}\right)^2 .
\end{equation}

Hence, all terms independent of \(\lambda_g\) can be grouped into \(C_g^t\), and
\(\widehat L_{\rho,g}^t(M_g,\lambda_g)\) can be written with respect to \(\lambda_g\) as
\begin{equation}
\frac{1}{2\nu_g}\lambda_g^2
+
\left(
\partial_{\lambda_g} f(\widetilde M_g^{t-1},\widetilde\lambda_g^{t-1})
-
\frac{1}{\nu_g}\widetilde\lambda_g^{t-1}
+
r_g
\right)\lambda_g
+
C_g^t.
\end{equation}

Combining the two expansions, and absorbing all terms independent of \((M_g,\lambda_g)\) into \(D_g^t\), we obtain
\begin{multline}
\widehat L_{\rho,g}^t(M_g,\lambda_g)
=
\left(\frac{1}{2\eta_g}+\frac{\rho}{2}\right)\|M_g\|_F^2
+
\frac{1}{2\nu_g}\lambda_g^2
\\
+
\Bigl\langle
\partial_{M_g} f(\widetilde M_g^{t-1},\widetilde\lambda_g^{t-1})
-
\frac{1}{\eta_g}\widetilde M_g^{t-1}
-
\rho\bigl(M^{t-1}-\mu_g^{t-1}\bigr),
\, M_g
\Bigr\rangle_F
\\
+
\left(
\partial_{\lambda_g} f(\widetilde M_g^{t-1},\widetilde\lambda_g^{t-1})
-
\frac{1}{\nu_g}\widetilde\lambda_g^{t-1}
+
r_g
\right)\lambda_g
+
D_g^t.
\end{multline}

Now apply Cauchy--Schwarz to the linear terms. We get
\begin{multline}
\Bigl\langle
\partial_{M_g} f(\widetilde M_g^{t-1},\widetilde\lambda_g^{t-1})
-
\frac{1}{\eta_g}\widetilde M_g^{t-1}
-
\rho\bigl(M^{t-1}-\mu_g^{t-1}\bigr),
\, M_g
\Bigr\rangle_F
\\
\ge
-
\left\|
\partial_{M_g} f(\widetilde M_g^{t-1},\widetilde\lambda_g^{t-1})
-
\frac{1}{\eta_g}\widetilde M_g^{t-1}
-
\rho\bigl(M^{t-1}-\mu_g^{t-1}\bigr)
\right\|_F
\|M_g\|_F,
\end{multline}
and
\begin{equation}
\left(
\partial_{\lambda_g} f(\widetilde M_g^{t-1},\widetilde\lambda_g^{t-1})
-
\frac{1}{\nu_g}\widetilde\lambda_g^{t-1}
+
r_g
\right)\lambda_g
\\
\ge
-
\left|
\partial_{\lambda_g} f(\widetilde M_g^{t-1},\widetilde\lambda_g^{t-1})
-
\frac{1}{\nu_g}\widetilde\lambda_g^{t-1}
+
r_g
\right|
\, |\lambda_g|.
\end{equation}

Therefore,
\begin{align}
\widehat L_{\rho,g}^t(M_g,\lambda_g)
\ge\;&
\left(\frac{1}{2\eta_g}+\frac{\rho}{2}\right)\|M_g\|_F^2
\nonumber\\
&\quad
-
\left\|
\partial_{M_g} f(\widetilde M_g^{t-1},\widetilde\lambda_g^{t-1})
-
\frac{1}{\eta_g}\widetilde M_g^{t-1}
\right.
\nonumber\\
&\qquad\qquad
\left.
-
\rho\bigl(M^{t-1}-\mu_g^{t-1}\bigr)
\right\|_F
\|M_g\|_F
\nonumber\\
&\quad
+
\frac{1}{2\nu_g}\lambda_g^2
-
\left|
\partial_{\lambda_g} f(\widetilde M_g^{t-1},\widetilde\lambda_g^{t-1})
-
\frac{1}{\nu_g}\widetilde\lambda_g^{t-1}
+
r_g
\right|
\, |\lambda_g|
+
D_g^t.
\end{align}

Since
\[
\frac{1}{2\eta_g}+\frac{\rho}{2}>0
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\frac{1}{2\nu_g}>0,
\]
the quadratic terms dominate the corresponding linear terms as
\[
\|M_g\|_F^2+|\lambda_g|^2\to\infty.
\]
Indeed,
\begin{align}
&\left(\frac{1}{2\eta_g}+\frac{\rho}{2}\right)\|M_g\|_F^2
-
\left\|
\partial_{M_g} f(\widetilde M_g^{t-1},\widetilde\lambda_g^{t-1})
-
\frac{1}{\eta_g}\widetilde M_g^{t-1}
\right.
\nonumber\\
&\qquad\qquad
\left.
-
\rho\bigl(M^{t-1}-\mu_g^{t-1}\bigr)
\right\|_F
\|M_g\|_F
\to\infty
\end{align}
as $\|M_g\|_F\to\infty$, and
\begin{equation}
\frac{1}{2\nu_g}\lambda_g^2
-
\left|
\partial_{\lambda_g} f(\widetilde M_g^{t-1},\widetilde\lambda_g^{t-1})
-
\frac{1}{\nu_g}\widetilde\lambda_g^{t-1}
+
r_g
\right|
\, |\lambda_g|
\to\infty
\end{equation}
as $|\lambda_g|\to\infty$. Hence,
\[
\widehat L_{\rho,g}^t(M_g,\lambda_g)\to\infty
\qquad\text{whenever}\qquad
\|M_g\|_F^2+|\lambda_g|^2\to\infty.
\]
Therefore, $\widehat L_{\rho,g}^t(M_g,\lambda_g)$ is coercive in $(M_g,\lambda_g)$.

label: lem:bounded_traj
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:bounded_traj}
Fix a finite training horizon $T\in \mathbb{N}$. Assume that, for each client $g$, the parameters satisfy
\[
\eta_g>0,\qquad \nu_g>0,\qquad \rho>0.
\]
Assume further that, for each client \(g=1,\dots,G\), the iterates are initialized as
\[
\widetilde M_g^0=0,\qquad
\widetilde\lambda_g^0=0,\qquad
\mu_g^0=0,\qquad
\tau_g^0=0,
\]
and that the global model is initialized as
\[
M^0=0.
\]
Then, for each $g$ and each $t=0,\dots,T$, the iterates
\[
\widetilde M_g^t,\qquad \widetilde\lambda_g^t,\qquad M^t,\qquad \mu_g^t,\qquad \tau_g^t
\]
are finite.

Consequently, the generated trajectory
\[
\mathcal T_T
:=
\left\{
(\widetilde M_g^t,\widetilde\lambda_g^t,M^t,\mu_g^t,\tau_g^t)
:\;
g=1,\dots,G,\; t=0,\dots,T
\right\}
\]
is a finite set, and therefore there exists a constant $E_T>0$ such that
\[
\|\widetilde M_g^t\|_F \le E_T,\qquad
|\widetilde\lambda_g^t| \le E_T,\qquad
\|M^t\|_F \le E_T,
\]
\[
\|\mu_g^t\|_F \le E_T,\qquad
|\tau_g^t| \le E_T,
\]
for all $g=1,\dots,G$ and all $t=0,\dots,T$.
head: environment
name: Finite-horizon boundedness of the generated trajectory

title: Proof
body_md:
We proceed by induction on the iteration index $t$.

For $t=0$, the initialization
\[
\widetilde M_g^0=0,\qquad
\widetilde\lambda_g^0=0,\qquad
M^0=0,\qquad
\mu_g^0=0,\qquad
\tau_g^0=0
\]
implies that all initial iterates are finite.

Now fix $t\in\{1,\dots,T\}$ and assume that, for every client $g$, the quantities
\[
\widetilde M_g^{t-1},\qquad \widetilde\lambda_g^{t-1},\qquad M^{t-1},\qquad \mu_g^{t-1},\qquad \tau_g^{t-1}
\]
are finite.By Lemma~\ref{lem:coercive}, for each client $g$, the local proximal linearized surrogate $\widehat L_{\rho,g}^t(M_g,\lambda_g)$
is coercive in $(M_g,\lambda_g)$. Since $\widehat L_{\rho,g}^t$ is also continuous in $(M_g,\lambda_g)$, it attains its minimum. Hence the local primal variables
\[
M_g^t,\qquad \lambda_g^t
\]
are finite for every client $g$, and so are the perturbed variables
\[
\widetilde M_g^t=M_g^t+\xi_g^t,\qquad \widetilde\lambda_g^t=\lambda_g^t+\zeta_g^t,
\]
since the Gaussian perturbations \(\xi_g^t\) and \(\zeta_g^t\) are finite.

Since the global model is updated according to
\[
M^t=\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g\bigl(\widetilde M_g^t+\mu_g^{t-1}\bigr),
\]
it follows that \(M^t\) is finite. Likewise, since the dual variable is updated as
\[
\mu_g^t=\mu_g^{t-1}+\widetilde M_g^t-M^t,
\]
it follows that \(\mu_g^t\) is finite. Finally, since
\[
\tau_g^t=\max\{0,\tau_g^{t-1}+\gamma(\phi(\widetilde M_g^t)-\widetilde\lambda_g^t)\},
\]
it follows that \(\tau_g^t\) is also finite, because it is obtained by applying finite-valued operations to previously computed finite quantities.

Thus, by induction, all iterates
\[
\widetilde M_g^t,\qquad \widetilde\lambda_g^t,\qquad M^t,\qquad \mu_g^t,\qquad \tau_g^t
\]
are finite for every $g=1,\dots,G$ and every $t=0,\dots,T$.

Since the index sets $\{1,\dots,G\}$ and $\{0,\dots,T\}$ are finite, the generated trajectory
\[
\mathcal T_T
=
\left\{
(\widetilde M_g^t,\widetilde\lambda_g^t,M^t,\mu_g^t,\tau_g^t)
:\;
g=1,\dots,G,\; t=0,\dots,T
\right\}
\]
contains finitely many points. Therefore, the maximum of the quantities
\[
\|\widetilde M_g^t\|_F,\qquad
|\widetilde\lambda_g^t|,\qquad
\|M^t\|_F,\qquad
\|\mu_g^t\|_F,\qquad
|\tau_g^t|
\]
over all $g=1,\dots,G$ and $t=0,\dots,T$ exists and is finite. Denote this maximum by $E_T$.

title: Proof
body_md:
Let \(v_g^t := (\widetilde M_g^t,\widetilde\lambda_g^t,M^t,\mu_g^t)\), and let $
\bar v_g^T := (\bar{\widetilde M}_g^T,\bar{\widetilde\lambda}_g^T,\bar M^T,\bar\mu_g^T)$
denote the corresponding average, where
\[
\bar{\widetilde M}_g^T := \frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\widetilde M_g^t,
\quad
\bar{\widetilde\lambda}_g^T := \frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\widetilde\lambda_g^t,
\quad
\bar M^T := \frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T M^t,
\quad
\bar\mu_g^T := \frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T \mu_g^t.
\]
Define
\[
H(v_g^t):=(\mu_g^t,\,0,\,-\mu_g^t,\,-(\widetilde M_g^t-M^t)).
\]
By direct expansion of the stacked inner product, we have
\begin{equation}
\langle v_g^t-v_g,\;H(v_g^t)\rangle
=
\langle \mu_g^t,\widetilde M_g^t-M_g\rangle_F
-\langle \mu_g^t,M^t-M\rangle_F
+\langle \mu_g-\mu_g^t,\widetilde M_g^t-M^t\rangle_F .
\label{eq:thm6_pf_1}
\end{equation}

To account for the update of $\tau_g$, write
\[
h_g^{t}(\cdot):=h_g(\cdot\,;\tau_g^{t-1})
\]
for the local objective used at round $t$, which is convex in $z_g$ for each fixed $\tau_g^{t-1}$.
Since $H$ is linear and monotone
\begin{equation}
\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g \langle \bar v_g^T-v_g,\;H(\bar v_g^T)\rangle
\le
\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\langle v_g^t-v_g,\;H(v_g^t)\rangle .
\label{eq:thm6_pf_3}
\end{equation}

Adding the per-round objective gaps to both sides of \eqref{eq:thm6_pf_3} and using
\eqref{eq:thm6_pf_1}, we obtain
\begin{multline}
\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\Bigl(h_g^{t}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})-h_g^{t}(z_g)\Bigr)
+\rho\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\langle \bar v_g^T-v_g,\;H(\bar v_g^T)\rangle
\\
\le
\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\Bigl(
h_g^{t}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})-h_g^{t}(z_g)
+\rho \langle v_g^t-v_g,\;H(v_g^t)\rangle
\Bigr)
\\
=
\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\Bigl(
h_g^{t}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})-h_g^{t}(z_g)
+\rho\langle \mu_g^t,\widetilde M_g^t-M_g\rangle_F
\\
\qquad
-\rho\langle \mu_g^t,M^t-M\rangle_F
+\rho\langle \mu_g-\mu_g^t,\widetilde M_g^t-M^t\rangle_F
\Bigr)
\\
=
\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\Bigl(
h_g^{t}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})-h_g^{t}(z_g)
+\rho\langle \mu_g^t,\widetilde M_g^t-M_g\rangle_F
\\
\qquad
+\rho\langle \mu_g-\mu_g^t,\widetilde M_g^t-M^t\rangle_F
\Bigr),
\label{eq:thm6_pf_4}
\end{multline}
where the last equality uses $\sum_{g=1}^G\alpha_g\mu_g^t=0$.


Applying Lemma 3 to each summand on the right-hand side of
\eqref{eq:thm6_pf_4} yields
\begin{multline}
\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\Bigl(h_g^{t}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})-h_g^{t}(z_g)\Bigr)
+\rho\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\langle \bar v_g^T-v_g,\;H(\bar v_g^T)\rangle
\\
\le
\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T
\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\Bigg[
\frac{\eta_g}{2}
\left\|
[h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})]_M
-\left(\rho+\frac{1}{\eta_g}\right)\xi_g^t
\right\|_F^2
+\frac{\nu_g}{2}
\left|
[h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})]_\lambda
-\frac{1}{\nu_g}\zeta_g^t
\right|^2
\\
\qquad
-\left(\rho+\frac{1}{\eta_g}\right)
\langle \xi_g^t,\,
M_g-\widetilde M_g^{\,t-1}\rangle_F
-\frac{1}{\nu_g}\,\zeta_g^t
\bigl(\lambda_g-\widetilde\lambda_g^{\,t-1}\bigr)
\\
\qquad
+\frac{1}{2\eta_g}
\Bigl(
\|M_g-\widetilde M_g^{\,t-1}\|_F^2
-\|M_g-\widetilde M_g^t\|_F^2
\Bigr)
\\
\qquad
+\frac{1}{2\nu_g}
\Bigl(
(\lambda_g-\widetilde\lambda_g^{\,t-1})^2
-(\lambda_g-\widetilde\lambda_g^t)^2
\Bigr)
\\
\qquad
+\frac{\rho}{2}
\Bigl(
\|M_g-M^{t-1}\|_F^2
-\|M_g-M^t\|_F^2
\Bigr)
+\frac{\rho}{2}
\Bigl(
\|\mu_g-\mu_g^{t-1}\|_F^2
-\|\mu_g-\mu_g^t\|_F^2
\Bigr)
\Bigg].
\label{eq:thm6_pf_5}
\end{multline}


Since the step sizes \(\eta_g\) and \(\nu_g\) are constant in \(t\), the
difference-of-squares terms in \eqref{eq:thm6_pf_5} telescope exactly, and
dropping the nonpositive terms
\(-\|M_g-\widetilde M_g^T\|_F^2\), \(-(\lambda_g-\widetilde\lambda_g^T)^2\),
\(-\|M_g-M^T\|_F^2\), and \(-\|\mu_g-\mu_g^T\|_F^2\) gives
\begin{multline}
\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\Bigl(h_g^{t}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})-h_g^{t}(z_g)\Bigr)
+\rho\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\langle \bar v_g^T-v_g,\;H(\bar v_g^T)\rangle
\\
\le
\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\Biggl[
\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T \frac{\eta_g}{2}
\left\|
[h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})]_M
-\left(\rho+\frac{1}{\eta_g}\right)\xi_g^t
\right\|_F^2
+\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T \frac{\nu_g}{2}
\left|
[h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})]_\lambda
-\frac{1}{\nu_g}\zeta_g^t
\right|^2
\\
\qquad
-\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T
\left(\rho+\frac{1}{\eta_g}\right)
\langle \xi_g^t,\;M_g-\widetilde M_g^{\,t-1}\rangle_F
-\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T
\frac{1}{\nu_g}\,\zeta_g^t\bigl(\lambda_g-\widetilde\lambda_g^{\,t-1}\bigr)
\\
\qquad
+\frac{1}{2T\eta_g}\|M_g-\widetilde M_g^0\|_F^2
+\frac{1}{2T\nu_g}(\lambda_g-\widetilde\lambda_g^0)^2
+\frac{\rho}{2T}\|M_g-M^0\|_F^2
+\frac{\rho}{2T}\|\mu_g-\mu_g^0\|_F^2
\Biggr].
\label{eq:thm6_pf_6}
\end{multline}


Next, choose the primal comparison point to be an optimal solution,
\[
z_g=z_g^\star=(M_g^\star,\lambda_g^\star),
\qquad
M_g^\star=M^\star \text{ for all } g,
\qquad
M=M^\star .
\]
With this choice, \eqref{eq:thm6_pf_6} becomes
\begin{multline}
\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\Bigl(h_g^{t}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})-h_g^{t}(z_g^\star)\Bigr)
+\rho\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\langle \bar v_g^T-v_g,\;H(\bar v_g^T)\rangle
\\
\le
\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\Biggl[
\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T \frac{\eta_g}{2}
\left\|
[h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})]_M
-\left(\rho+\frac{1}{\eta_g}\right)\xi_g^t
\right\|_F^2
+\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T \frac{\nu_g}{2}
\left|
[h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})]_\lambda
-\frac{1}{\nu_g}\zeta_g^t
\right|^2
\\
\qquad
-\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T
\left(\rho+\frac{1}{\eta_g}\right)
\langle \xi_g^t,\;M^\star-\widetilde M_g^{\,t-1}\rangle_F
-\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T
\frac{1}{\nu_g}\,\zeta_g^t\bigl(\lambda_g^\star-\widetilde\lambda_g^{\,t-1}\bigr)
\\
\qquad
+\frac{1}{2T\eta_g}\|M^\star-\widetilde M_g^0\|_F^2
+\frac{1}{2T\nu_g}(\lambda_g^\star-\widetilde\lambda_g^0)^2
+\frac{\rho}{2T}\|M^\star-M^0\|_F^2
+\frac{\rho}{2T}\|\mu_g-\mu_g^0\|_F^2
\Biggr],
\label{eq:thm6_pf_7}
\end{multline}
where \(v_g=(M^\star,\lambda_g^\star,M^\star,\mu_g)\).




Take the initialization
\[
M^0=0,
\qquad
\widetilde M_g^0=0,
\qquad
\widetilde\lambda_g^0=0,
\qquad
\mu_g^0=0
\quad \text{for all } g.
\]


Then \eqref{eq:thm6_pf_7} simplifies to
\begin{multline}
\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\Bigl(h_g^{t}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})-h_g^{t}(z_g^\star)\Bigr)
+\rho\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\langle \bar v_g^T-v_g,\;H(\bar v_g^T)\rangle
\\
\le
\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g \frac{\eta_g}{2}
\left\|
[h_g'(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})]_M
-\left(\rho+\frac{1}{\eta_g}\right)\xi_g^t
\right\|_F^2
+\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g \frac{\nu_g}{2}
\left|
[h_g'(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})]_\lambda
-\frac{1}{\nu_g}\zeta_g^t
\right|^2
\\
\qquad
-\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\left(\rho+\frac{1}{\eta_g}\right)
\langle \xi_g^t,\;M^\star-\widetilde M_g^{\,t-1}\rangle_F
-\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\frac{1}{\nu_g}\,\zeta_g^t\bigl(\lambda_g^\star-\widetilde\lambda_g^{\,t-1}\bigr)
\\
\qquad
+\frac{\|M^\star\|_F^2}{T}\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g \frac{1}{2\eta_g}
+\frac{1}{T}\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g \frac{(\lambda_g^\star)^2}{2\nu_g}
+\frac{\rho}{2T}\|M^\star\|_F^2
+\frac{\rho}{2T}\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g \|\mu_g\|_F^2 .
\label{eq:thm6_pf_8}
\end{multline}


We now simplify the term \(\rho \langle \bar v_g^T-v_g,\;H(\bar v_g^T)\rangle\).
For a comparison point \(v_g=(M,\lambda_g,M,\mu_g)\), we have
\begin{multline}
\langle \bar v_g^T-v_g,\;H(\bar v_g^T)\rangle
=
\langle \bar\mu_g^T,\bar{\widetilde M}_g^T-M\rangle_F
-\langle \bar\mu_g^T,\bar M^T-M\rangle_F
-\langle \bar\mu_g^T-\mu_g,\bar{\widetilde M}_g^T-\bar M^T\rangle_F
\\
=
\langle \mu_g,\bar{\widetilde M}_g^T-\bar M^T\rangle_F.
\label{eq:thm6_pf_9}
\end{multline}
Therefore, the left-hand side of \eqref{eq:thm6_pf_8} equals
\begin{equation}
\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\Bigl(h_g^{t}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})-h_g^{t}(z_g^\star)\Bigr)
+\rho\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\langle \mu_g,\bar{\widetilde M}_g^T-\bar M^T\rangle_F .
\label{eq:thm6_pf_10}
\end{equation}

Now restrict the comparison dual variable to the ball
\[
\{\mu_g:\|\mu_g\|_F\le \beta/\rho\}.
\]
Let
\[
d_g^T:=\bar{\widetilde M}_g^T-\bar M^T.
\]
By Cauchy--Schwarz,
\begin{equation}
\max_{\|\mu_g\|_F\le \beta/\rho}
\rho\langle \mu_g,d_g^T\rangle_F
\le
\rho \max_{\|\mu_g\|_F\le \beta/\rho}
\|\mu_g\|_F\,\|d_g^T\|_F
=
\beta \|d_g^T\|_F.
\label{eq:thm6_pf_11}
\end{equation}


The bound is tight by choosing
\[
\hat\mu_g = \frac{\beta}{\rho}\frac{d_g^T}{\|d_g^T\|_F}
\qquad \text{when } d_g^T\neq 0,
\]
hence
\begin{equation}
\max_{\|\mu_g\|_F\le \beta/\rho}
\rho\langle \mu_g,\bar{\widetilde M}_g^T-\bar M^T\rangle_F
=
\beta \|\bar{\widetilde M}_g^T-\bar M^T\|_F.
\label{eq:thm6_pf_12}
\end{equation}

Consequently, using \eqref{eq:thm6_pf_10} and \eqref{eq:thm6_pf_12},
\begin{multline}
\max_{\substack{\|\mu_g\|_F\le \beta/\rho\\ g=1,\dots,G}}
\Biggl[
\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\Bigl(h_g^{t}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})-h_g^{t}(z_g^\star)\Bigr)
+\rho\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\langle \bar v_g^T-v_g,\;H(\bar v_g^T)\rangle
\Biggr]
\\
=
\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\Bigl(h_g^{t}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})-h_g^{t}(z_g^\star)\Bigr)
+\beta\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\|\bar{\widetilde M}_g^T-\bar M^T\|_F .
\label{eq:thm6_pf_13}
\end{multline}
We now maximize the last term on the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:thm6_pf_8}
over the same ball. Since \(\|\mu_g\|_F\le \beta/\rho\) and \(\sum_{g=1}^G\alpha_g=1\),
\begin{equation}
\max_{\substack{\|\mu_g\|_F\le \beta/\rho\\ g=1,\dots,G}}
\frac{\rho}{2T}\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g \|\mu_g\|_F^2
\le
\frac{\rho}{2T}\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g \frac{\beta^2}{\rho^2}
=
\frac{\beta^2}{2\rho T}.
\label{eq:thm6_pf_14}
\end{equation}


Since \eqref{eq:thm6_pf_8} holds for every \(\mu_g\), we may take the maximum
over \(\|\mu_g\|_F\le\beta/\rho\), \(g=1,\dots,G\), on both sides. Using
\eqref{eq:thm6_pf_13} for the left-hand side and \eqref{eq:thm6_pf_14} for the
only \(\mu_g\)-dependent term on the right-hand side, we obtain
\begin{multline}
\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\Bigl(h_g^{t}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})-h_g^{t}(z_g^\star)\Bigr)
+\beta\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\|\bar{\widetilde M}_g^T-\bar M^T\|_F
\\
\le
\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g \frac{\eta_g}{2}
\left\|
[h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})]_M
-\left(\rho+\frac{1}{\eta_g}\right)\xi_g^t
\right\|_F^2
+\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g \frac{\nu_g}{2}
\left|
[h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})]_\lambda
-\frac{1}{\nu_g}\zeta_g^t
\right|^2
\\
\qquad
-\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\left(\rho+\frac{1}{\eta_g}\right)
\langle \xi_g^t,\;M^\star-\widetilde M_g^{\,t-1}\rangle_F
-\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\frac{1}{\nu_g}\,\zeta_g^t\bigl(\lambda_g^\star-\widetilde\lambda_g^{\,t-1}\bigr)
\\
\qquad
+\frac{\|M^\star\|_F^2}{T}\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g \frac{1}{2\eta_g}
+\frac{1}{2T}\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\frac{(\lambda_g^\star)^2}{\nu_g}
+\frac{\rho}{2T}\|M^\star\|_F^2
+\frac{\beta^2}{2\rho T}.
\label{eq:thm6_pf_15}
\end{multline}


We now take expectations on both sides of \eqref{eq:thm6_pf_15}. By construction
of Algorithm~2, for each \(g\) and \(t\), the perturbations \(\xi_g^t\) and
\(\zeta_g^t\) are drawn independently of each other and of all past iterates, and satisfy
\[
\mathbb{E}[\xi_g^t]=0,\qquad
\mathbb{E}\|\xi_g^t\|_F^2=KP\,\sigma_{M,g}^2,\qquad
\mathbb{E}[\zeta_g^t]=0,\qquad
\mathbb{E}(\zeta_g^t)^2=\sigma_{\lambda,g}^2 .
\]
Since \(M^\star-\widetilde M_g^{\,t-1}\) and \(\lambda_g^\star-\widetilde\lambda_g^{\,t-1}\)
depend only on past iterates, while \(\xi_g^t\) and \(\zeta_g^t\) are independent of the
past and have zero mean, it follows that
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{E}\langle \xi_g^t,\; M^\star-\widetilde M_g^{\,t-1}\rangle_F=0,
\qquad
\mathbb{E}\bigl[\zeta_g^t\,(\lambda_g^\star-\widetilde\lambda_g^{\,t-1})\bigr]=0.
\label{eq:thm6_pf_16}
\end{equation}

Recall that, at round \(t\),
\[
h_g^{t}(z_g)=\lambda_g r_g+\frac{1}{N_g}\sum_{n=1}^{N_g}L_n(M_g,\lambda_g)+R_g(M_g,\lambda_g;\tau_g^{t-1}),
\qquad z_g=(M_g,\lambda_g),
\]
where
\[
L_n(M_g,\lambda_g)
:=
\max_{y\in\mathcal Y}
\Bigl(
\ell_{\mathrm{CS}}(M_g;x_n,y)-\kappa\lambda_g\,\mathbf{1}_{\{y\neq y_n\}}
\Bigr),
\]
and
\[
R_g(M_g,\lambda_g;\tau_g^{t-1})
:=
\frac{1}{2\gamma}
\Bigl(
\max\{0,\tau_g^{t-1}+\gamma(\phi(M_g)-\lambda_g)\}^2-(\tau_g^{t-1})^2
\Bigr).
\]

Next, define
\[
a_g^{t-1}:=[h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})]_M,
\qquad
b_g^{t-1}:=[h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})]_\lambda,
\qquad
c_g:=\rho+\frac{1}{\eta_g}.
\]
By direct evaluation of the selected subgradients of the robust loss term,
\[
\|\partial_{M_g}L_n(M_g,\lambda_g)\|_F \le \sqrt{2}\,L,
\qquad
\partial_{\lambda_g}L_n(M_g,\lambda_g)\in[-\kappa,0].
\]
Since \([h_g^{t\prime}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})]_\lambda
= r_g+\frac{1}{N_g}\sum_{n=1}^{N_g}\partial_{\lambda_g}L_n+\partial_{\lambda_g}R_g\),
the first two terms together lie in \([r_g-\kappa,\,r_g]\), so that
\[
\Bigl|\,r_g+\frac{1}{N_g}\sum_{n=1}^{N_g}\partial_{\lambda_g}L_n\Bigr|
\le S:=\max\{r_g,\ \kappa-r_g\}.
\]


Moreover, since
\(\partial_{\lambda_g}R_g=-\max\{0,\tau_g^{t-1}+\gamma(\phi(M_g)-\lambda_g)\}\) and
\(\partial_{M_g}R_g=\max\{0,\tau_g^{t-1}+\gamma(\phi(M_g)-\lambda_g)\}\,\partial\phi(M_g)\),
using \(\phi(M_g)\le\sqrt{2}\,\|M_g\|_F\) and \(\|\partial\phi(M_g)\|_F\le C_\phi\) gives
\[
\|\partial_{M_g}R_g(M_g,\lambda_g;\tau_g^{t-1})\|_F
\le
\bigl(|\tau_g^{t-1}|+\gamma\sqrt{2}\,\|M_g\|_F+\gamma[-\lambda_g]_+\bigr)C_\phi,
\]
and
\[
|\partial_{\lambda_g}R_g(M_g,\lambda_g;\tau_g^{t-1})|
\le
|\tau_g^{t-1}|+\gamma\sqrt{2}\,\|M_g\|_F+\gamma[-\lambda_g]_+ .
\]

Further, Lemma~\ref{lem:bounded_traj} shows that the trajectory generated by Algorithm~2 remains finite
over the training horizon, so that the penalty subgradients evaluated along it are
bounded. Accordingly, we assume that these bounds are uniform: there exist constants
\(C,V>0\) such that
\[
\bigl\|\partial_{M_g}R_g(\widetilde M_g^{\,t-1},\widetilde\lambda_g^{\,t-1};\tau_g^{t-1})\bigr\|_F
\le \sqrt{2}\,C,
\qquad
\bigl|\partial_{\lambda_g}R_g(\widetilde M_g^{\,t-1},\widetilde\lambda_g^{\,t-1};\tau_g^{t-1})\bigr|
\le V,
\]
for all \(g=1,\dots,G\) and \(t=1,\dots,T\).

Therefore,
\begin{equation}
\|a_g^{t-1}\|_F \le \sqrt{2}\,(L+C),
\qquad
|b_g^{t-1}| \le S+V.
\label{eq:thm6_pf_17}
\end{equation}

Expanding the square and using that \(\xi_g^t\) is zero-mean and independent of
\(a_g^{t-1}\), which depends only on past iterates, gives
\begin{equation}
\mathbb E\|a_g^{t-1}-c_g\xi_g^t\|_F^2
=
\mathbb E\|a_g^{t-1}\|_F^2
-2c_g\,\mathbb E\langle a_g^{t-1},\xi_g^t\rangle_F
+c_g^2\,\mathbb E\|\xi_g^t\|_F^2
=
\mathbb E\|a_g^{t-1}\|_F^2 + c_g^2 KP\,\sigma_{M,g}^2 ,
\end{equation}
and likewise, since \(\zeta_g^t\) is zero-mean and independent of \(b_g^{t-1}\),
\begin{equation}
\mathbb E\Bigl|b_g^{t-1}-\frac{1}{\nu_g}\zeta_g^t\Bigr|^2
=
\mathbb E|b_g^{t-1}|^2+\frac{\sigma_{\lambda,g}^2}{\nu_g^2} .
\end{equation}
Using \eqref{eq:thm6_pf_17}, we obtain
\begin{equation}
\mathbb E\|a_g^{t-1}-c_g\xi_g^t\|_F^2
\le
2(L+C)^2 + c_g^2 KP\,\sigma_{M,g}^2,
\qquad
\mathbb E\Bigl|b_g^{t-1}-\frac{1}{\nu_g}\zeta_g^t\Bigr|^2
\le
(S+V)^2+\frac{\sigma_{\lambda,g}^2}{\nu_g^2} .
\label{eq:thm6_pf_18}
\end{equation}


Taking expectations in \eqref{eq:thm6_pf_15} and using
\eqref{eq:thm6_pf_16}, \eqref{eq:thm6_pf_17}, and \eqref{eq:thm6_pf_18}, we get
\begin{multline}
\mathbb E\Biggl[
\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\Bigl(h_g^{t}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})-h_g^{t}(z_g^\star)\Bigr)
+\beta\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\|\bar{\widetilde M}_g^T-\bar M^T\|_F
\Biggr]
\\
\le
\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\frac{\eta_g}{2}
\Biggl(
2(L+C)^2+\left(\rho+\frac{1}{\eta_g}\right)^2 KP\,\sigma_{M,g}^2
\Biggr)
+
\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\frac{\nu_g}{2}
\Biggl(
(S+V)^2+\frac{\sigma_{\lambda,g}^2}{\nu_g^2}
\Biggr)
\\
+\frac{\|M^\star\|_F^2}{T}\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g \frac{1}{2\eta_g}
+\frac{1}{2T}\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\frac{(\lambda_g^\star)^2}{\nu_g}
+\frac{\rho}{2T}\|M^\star\|_F^2
+\frac{\beta^2}{2\rho T}.
\label{eq:thm6_pf_19}
\end{multline}

Now substitute the DP-calibrated Gaussian variances from Theorem~1,
\[
\sigma_{M,g}^2
=
\frac{8L^2}{N_g^2\left(\rho+\frac{1}{\eta_g}\right)^2}
\frac{2\ln(1.25/\delta_M)}{\epsilon_M^2},
\qquad
\sigma_{\lambda,g}^2
=
\frac{\kappa^2\nu_g^2}{N_g^2}
\frac{2\ln(1.25/\delta_\lambda)}{\epsilon_\lambda^2}.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
\left(\rho+\frac{1}{\eta_g}\right)^2 KP\,\sigma_{M,g}^2
=
KP\cdot \frac{8L^2}{N_g^2}\cdot \frac{2\ln(1.25/\delta_M)}{\epsilon_M^2},
\qquad
\frac{\sigma_{\lambda,g}^2}{\nu_g^2}
=
\frac{\kappa^2}{N_g^2}\cdot\frac{2\ln(1.25/\delta_\lambda)}{\epsilon_\lambda^2}.
\label{eq:thm6_pf_20}
\end{equation}

Substituting \eqref{eq:thm6_pf_20} into \eqref{eq:thm6_pf_19} yields
\begin{multline}
\mathbb E\Biggl[
\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\Bigl(h_g^{t}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})-h_g^{t}(z_g^\star)\Bigr)
+\beta\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\|\bar{\widetilde M}_g^T-\bar M^T\|_F
\Biggr]
\\
\le
\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\frac{\eta_g}{2}
\left(
2(L+C)^2
+
KP\cdot \frac{8L^2}{N_g^2}\cdot \frac{2\ln(1.25/\delta_M)}{\epsilon_M^2}
\right)
+
\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\frac{\nu_g}{2}
\left(
(S+V)^2
+
\frac{\kappa^2}{N_g^2}\cdot\frac{2\ln(1.25/\delta_\lambda)}{\epsilon_\lambda^2}
\right)
\\
+\frac{\|M^\star\|_F^2}{T}\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g \frac{1}{2\eta_g}
+\frac{1}{2T}\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\frac{(\lambda_g^\star)^2}{\nu_g}
+\frac{\rho}{2T}\|M^\star\|_F^2
+\frac{\beta^2}{2\rho T}.
\label{eq:thm6_pf_21}
\end{multline}

For constants \(c_M,c_{\lambda,g}>0\) satisfying \(\|M^\star\|_F\le c_M\) and
\(|\lambda_g^\star|\le c_{\lambda,g}\) for all \(g\), define the \(M_g\)-block and
\(\lambda_g\)-block step sizes as
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\eta_g
&:=
\frac{c_M}
{
\sqrt{
T\left(
2(L+C)^2
+
KP\cdot \frac{8L^2}{N_g^2}\cdot \frac{2\ln(1.25/\delta_M)}{\epsilon_M^2}
\right)
}
},
\\
\nu_g
&:=
\frac{c_{\lambda,g}}
{
\sqrt{
T\left(
(S+V)^2
+
\frac{\kappa^2}{N_g^2}\cdot\frac{2\ln(1.25/\delta_\lambda)}{\epsilon_\lambda^2}
\right)
}
}.
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:thm6_pf_22}
\end{equation}
For convenience, define
\begin{equation}
D_{M,g}
:=
\sqrt{
2(L+C)^2
+
KP\cdot \frac{8L^2}{N_g^2}\cdot \frac{2\ln(1.25/\delta_M)}{\epsilon_M^2}
},
\qquad
D_{\lambda,g}
:=
\sqrt{
(S+V)^2
+
\frac{\kappa^2}{N_g^2}\cdot\frac{2\ln(1.25/\delta_\lambda)}{\epsilon_\lambda^2}
}.
\label{eq:thm6_pf_23}
\end{equation}

Substituting \eqref{eq:thm6_pf_22} into \eqref{eq:thm6_pf_21} and using
\(\|M^\star\|_F^2\le c_M^2\) and \((\lambda_g^\star)^2\le c_{\lambda,g}^2\), we obtain
\begin{multline}
\mathbb E\Biggl[
\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\Bigl(h_g^{t}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})-h_g^{t}(z_g^\star)\Bigr)
+\beta\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\|\bar{\widetilde M}_g^T-\bar M^T\|_F
\Biggr]
\\
\le
\frac{1}{\sqrt T}\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g\, c_M D_{M,g}
+
\frac{1}{\sqrt T}\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g\, c_{\lambda,g} D_{\lambda,g}
+
\frac{\rho}{2T}c_M^2
+\frac{\beta^2}{2\rho T}.
\label{eq:thm6_pf_24}
\end{multline}


Defining
\begin{equation}
M_{1,T}
:=
\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g\, c_M D_{M,g}
+
\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g\, c_{\lambda,g} D_{\lambda,g},
\qquad
M_2
:=
\frac{\rho}{2}c_M^2+\frac{\beta^2}{2\rho},
\label{eq:thm6_pf_26}
\end{equation}
we can rewrite (122) as
\begin{multline}
\mathbb E\Biggl[
\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\Bigl(h_g^{t}(\widetilde z_g^{\,t-1})-h_g^{t}(z_g^\star)\Bigr)
+\beta\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g
\|\bar{\widetilde M}_g^T-\bar M^T\|_F
\Biggr]
\\
\le
\frac{1}{\sqrt T}
\Biggl[
\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g\, c_M D_{M,g}
+
\sum_{g=1}^G \alpha_g\, c_{\lambda,g} D_{\lambda,g}
\Biggr]
+
\frac{1}{T}
\Bigl(
\frac{\rho}{2}c_M^2+\frac{\beta^2}{2\rho}
\Bigr)
=
\frac{M_{1,T}}{\sqrt T}+\frac{M_2}{T}.
\label{eq:thm6_pf_27}
\end{multline}
This proves the claimed convergence bound.
